classification.difficultyReason: Justify a viewing angle, use sine rule for a sloping length, then right-triangle trigonometry for height.

content.prompt: The angles of elevation of a building measured from two positions 80 m apart are $32^\circ$ and $55^\circ$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6 building and two sight lines
spec.description: A, B, D lie left to right on the horizontal ground; T lies above D. Blue ground and sight lines; red rectangular building extends right of DT with pale orange-red fill and a regular window grid. Right-angle marker remains at the building's bottom-right corner. Source angle labels have no drawn arcs.
spec.mathematics: AB=80 m, angle TAD=32 degrees, angle TBD=55 degrees, DT=h. No derived lengths appear.

answer.worked:
The exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
$$\begin{align*}55^\circ&=32^\circ+\angle ATB\\\angle ATB&=55^\circ-32^\circ\\\angle ATB&=23^\circ\end{align*}$$
